01 / COMPOSITIONSEEDED

BLENDREGIONS + OVERLAYS

Regions share the page, and their amounts set each one's share. Overlays draw across the regions over their own share of the page. A wider transition lets one motif thin out as the next fills in.

    BEFORE THE FIRST PLOT
    
  
    From screen to paper.
    
  
    The SVG has physical dimensions in millimetres and contains stroked paths grouped by pen. It has no embedded raster, filled areas, live text, or paper background.
    
  
      
    
    1. Open the SVG in your plotter software or Inkscape. Confirm page dimensions and your iDraw’s usable drawing area.
      2. 
    
    2. Plot one pen layer at a time. Use “Export pens separately” for one full-page SVG per colour. In a blend, give a motif its own pen to plot it as a separate pass. A diagram draws its ink on pen 1 and its red on pen 2.
      3. 
    
    3. Start with a small proof. Nominal spacing is not a minimum clearance guarantee: displaced lines, overlays, growth strands and secondary lines can overlap.
      4. 
    
    4. The displayed pen width previews your nib; the physical mark depends on your pen. Sorting preserves geometry, but downstream software may reorder paths.
      5. 
  
    
  
    Time estimates use line length, travel length, and a lift delay. Acceleration, homing, pen changes, and controller overhead are excluded.
    
  
    Save a recipe to recreate a drawing. Recipes from version 0.1 load as a single motif.
